selected_passages.title: sources/News_publisher_files_class_action_antitrust_suit_against_Google_citing_AI_s_harms_to_their_bottom_line
selected_passages.text: Helena World Chronicle, LLC has filed a class action antitrust lawsuit against Google and Alphabet in the U.S. District Court in D.C., alleging that Google's AI technologies, including Search Generative Experience (SGE) and Bard, along with older features like the Knowledge Graph, are siphoning content, readers, and ad revenue from news publishers. The suit claims these practices violate the Sherman Act and Clayton Act by discouraging users from visiting publisher websites, potentially causing publishers to lose 20-40% of their traffic, and seeks an injunction requiring consent for using publisher data to train AI models.

selected_passages.title: sources/News_publisher_files_class_action_antitrust_suit_against_Google_citing_AI_s_harms_to_their_bottom_line
selected_passages.text:
- Helena World Chronicle filed a class action antitrust suit against Google and Alphabet in the U.S. District Court in D.C.
- The lawsuit alleges Google uses AI technologies like SGE and Bard to misappropriate publisher content and reduce traffic to news sites.
- Plaintiffs claim Google's actions violate the Sherman Act and Clayton Act, seeking monetary and injunctive relief.
- Reports suggest publishers could lose 20-40% of website traffic when Google's AI products fully roll out.
- The case follows a recent agreement where Google pays Canadian media $73.5 million annually for content use.
